verses.1: In the land of Uz 1 there was a blameless and upright man named Job, who feared God and avoided evil.
verses.2: 2 Seven sons and three daughters were born to him;
verses.3: 3 and he had seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred she-asses, and a great number of work animals, so that he was greater than any of the men of the East.
verses.4: His sons used to take turns giving feasts, sending invitations to their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
verses.5: And when each feast had run its course, Job would send for them and sanctify them, rising early and offering holocausts for every one of them. For Job said, "It may be that my sons have sinned and blasphemed God in their hearts." This Job did habitually.
verses.6: 4 One day, when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, Satan also came among them.
verses.7: And the LORD said to Satan, "Whence do you come?" Then Satan answered the LORD and said, "From roaming the earth and patrolling it."
verses.8: And the LORD said to Satan, "Have you noticed my servant Job, and that there is no one on earth like him, blameless and upright, fearing God and avoiding evil?"
verses.9: But Satan answered the LORD and said, "Is it for nothing that Job is God-fearing?
verses.10: Have you not surrounded him and his family and all that he has with your protection? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock are spread over the land.
verses.11: But now put forth your hand and touch anything that he has, and surely he will blaspheme you to your face."
verses.12: And the LORD said to Satan, "Behold, all that he has is in your power; only do not lay a hand upon his person." So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD.
verses.13: And so one day, while his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their eldest brother,
verses.14: a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing and the asses grazing beside them,
verses.15: 5 and the Sabeans carried them off in a raid. They put the herdsmen to the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
verses.16: 6 While he was yet speaking, another came and said, "Lightning has fallen from heaven and struck the sheep and their shepherds and consumed them; and I alone have escaped to tell you."
verses.17: While he was yet speaking, another came and said, "The Chaldeans formed three columns, seized the camels, carried them off, and put those tending them to the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
verses.18: While he was yet speaking, another came and said, "Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their eldest brother,
verses.19: when suddenly a great wind came across the desert and smote the four corners of the house. It fell upon the young people and they are dead; and I alone have escaped to tell you."
verses.20: Then Job began to tear his cloak and cut off his hair. He cast himself prostrate upon the ground,
verses.21: 7 and said, "Naked I came forth from my mother's womb, and naked shall I go back again. The LORD gave and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD!"
verses.22: In all this Job did not sin, nor did he say anything disrespectful of God. 1 [1] Uz: somewhere in Edom or Arabia. Job: a not uncommon name in ancient Semitic circles; its original meaning was "enemy." 2 [2-3] The numbers mentioned here indicate Job's great wealth and happiness, external proof of God's friendship. 3 [3] Men of the East: that is, east of Palestine. 4 [6] Sons of God: angels. Satan: literally, "adversary." 5 [15] Sabeans: from southern Arabia. 6 [16] Lightning: literally, "God's fire." 7 [21] Go back again: to the earth; cf ⇒ Genesis 2:7; ⇒ Sirach 40:1. verses.23: Once again the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them.
verses.24: And the LORD said to Satan, "Whence do you come?" And Satan answered the LORD and said, "From roaming the earth and patrolling it."
verses.25: And the LORD said to Satan, "Have you noticed my servant Job, and that there is no one on earth like him, faultless and upright, fearing God and avoiding evil? He still holds fast to his innocence although you incited me against him to ruin him without cause."
verses.26: 1 And Satan answered the LORD and said, "Skin for skin! All that a man has will he give for his life.
verses.27: But now put forth your hand and touch his bone and his flesh, and surely he will blaspheme you to your face."
verses.28: And the LORD said to Satan, "He is in your power; only spare his life."
verses.29: So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD and smote Job with severe boils from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head.
verses.30: And he took a potsherd to scrape himself, as he sat among the ashes.
verses.31: 2 Then his wife said to him, "Are you still holding to your innocence? Curse God and die."
verses.32: But he said to her, "Are even you going to speak as senseless women do? We accept good things from God; and should we not accept evil?" Through all this, Job said nothing sinful.
verses.33: 3 Now when three of Job's friends heard of all the misfortune that had come upon him, they set out each one from his own place: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuh, and Zophar from Naamath. They met and journeyed together to give him sympathy and comfort.
verses.34: But when, at a distance, they lifted up their eyes and did not recognize him, they began to weep aloud; they tore their cloaks and threw dust upon their heads.
verses.35: Then they sat down upon the ground with him seven days and seven nights, but none of them spoke a word to him; for they saw how great was his suffering. 1 [4] Skin for skin: an expression which, as applied to Job, means that he has borne his suffering patiently thus far only because he seeks to avoid greater suffering and to receive greater favors from God. 2 [9] Curse God and die: you have nothing to hope for from God and therefore nothing to live for. 3 [11] The names of Job's friends suggest Edomite origin. The Edomites ( ⇒ Obadiah 1:8-9) and more specifically the Temanites ( ⇒ Jeremiah 49:7) enjoyed a reputation for wisdom. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.62: Then spoke Eliphaz the Temanite, who said:
verses.63: If someone attempts a word with you, will you mind? For how can anyone refrain from speaking?
verses.64: Behold, you have instructed many, and have made firm their feeble hands.
verses.65: Your words have upheld the stumbler; you have strengthened his faltering knees.
verses.66: But now that it comes to you, you are impatient; when it touches yourself, you are dismayed.
verses.67: Is not your piety a source of confidence, and your integrity of life your hope?
verses.68: Reflect now, what innocent person perishes? Since when are the upright destroyed?
verses.69: As I see it, those who plow for mischief and sow trouble, reap the same.
verses.70: By the breath of God they perish, and by the blast of his wrath they are consumed.
verses.71: 1 Though the lion roars, though the king of beasts cries out, yet the teeth of the young lions are broken;
verses.72: The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
verses.73: 2 For a word was stealthily brought to me, and my ear caught a whisper of it.
verses.74: In my thoughts during visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,
verses.75: Fear came upon me, and shuddering, that terrified me to the bones.
verses.76: Then a spirit passed before me, and the hair of my flesh stood up.
verses.77: It paused, but its likeness I could not discern; a figure was before my eyes, and I heard a still voice:
verses.78: "Can a man be righteous as against God? Can a mortal be blameless against his Maker?
verses.79: Lo, he puts no trust in his servants, and with his angels he can find fault.
verses.80: How much more with those that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed more easily than the moth!
verses.81: Morning or evening they may be shattered; with no heed paid to it, they perish forever.
verses.82: The pegs of their tent are plucked up; they die without knowing wisdom." 1 [10] The lion: used figuratively here for the violent, rapacious sinner who cannot prevail against God. 2 [12-21] A dramatic presentation of the idea of man's nothingness in contrast to God's greatness. verses.111: Ah, could my anguish but be measured and my calamity laid with it in the scales,
verses.112: They would now outweigh the sands of the sea! Because of this I speak without restraint.
verses.113: For the arrows of the Almighty pierce me, and my spirit drinks in their poison; the terrors of God are arrayed against me.
verses.114: 1 Does the wild ass bray when he has grass? Does the ox low over his fodder?
verses.115: Can a thing insipid be eaten without salt? Is there flavor in the white of an egg?
verses.116: I refuse to touch them; they are loathsome food to me.
verses.117: Oh, that I might have my request, and that God would grant what I long for:
verses.118: Even that God would decide to crush me, that he would put forth his hand and cut me off!
verses.119: Then I should still have consolation and could exult through unremitting pain, because I have not transgressed the commands of the Holy One.
verses.120: What strength have I that I should endure, and what is my limit that I should be patient?
verses.121: Have I the strength of stones, or is my flesh of bronze?
verses.122: Have I no helper, and has advice deserted me?
verses.123: A friend owes kindness to one in despair, though he have forsaken the fear of the Almighty.
verses.124: My brethren are undependable as a brook, as watercourses that run dry in the wadies;
verses.125: Though they may be black with ice, and with snow heaped upon them,
verses.126: Yet once they flow, they cease to be; in the heat, they disappear from their place.
verses.127: Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go into the desert and perish.
verses.128: 2 The caravans of Tema search, the companies of Sheba have hopes;
verses.129: They are disappointed, though they were confident; they come there and are frustrated.
verses.130: It is thus that you have now become for me; you see a terrifying thing and are afraid.
verses.131: Have I asked you to give me anything, to offer a gift for me from your possessions,
verses.132: Or to deliver me from the enemy, or to redeem me from oppressors?
verses.133: Teach me, and I will be silent; prove to me wherein I have erred.
verses.134: How agreeable are honest words; yet how unconvincing is your argument!
verses.135: Do you consider your words as proof, but the sayings of a desperate man as wind?
verses.136: You would even cast lots for the orphan, and would barter away your friend!
verses.137: Come, now, give me your attention; surely I will not lie to your face.
verses.138: Think it over; let there be no injustice. Think it over; I still am right.
verses.139: Is there insincerity on my tongue, or cannot my taste discern falsehood? 1 [5-6] Job would not complain if his life were as pleasant to him as fodder to a hungry animal; but his life is as disagreeable as insipid food. White of an egg: thus the obscure Hebrew has been understood in Jewish tradition; some render it "mallow juice." 2 [19] Tema: in northwest Arabia. Sheba: see note on ⇒ Job 1:15. verses.140: 1 Is not man's life on earth a drudgery? Are not his days those of a hireling?
verses.141: He is a slave who longs for the shade, a hireling who waits for his wages.
verses.142: So I have been assigned months of misery, and troubled nights have been told off for me.
verses.143: If in bed I say, "When shall I arise?" then the night drags on; I am filled with restlessness until the dawn.
verses.144: My flesh is clothed with worms and scabs; my skin cracks and festers;
verses.145: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle; they come to an end without hope.
verses.146: Remember that my life is like the wind; I shall not see happiness again.
verses.147: The eye that now sees me shall no more behold me; as you look at me, I shall be gone.
verses.148: As a cloud dissolves and vanishes, so he who goes down to the nether world shall come up no more.
verses.149: He shall not again return to his house; his place shall know him no more.
verses.150: My own utterance I will not restrain; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.151: 2 3 Am I the sea, or a monster of the deep, that you place a watch over me? Why have you set me up as an object of attack; or why should I be a target for you?
verses.152: When I say, "My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint,"
verses.153: Then you affright me with dreams and with visions terrify me,
verses.154: So that I should prefer choking and death rather than my pains.
verses.155: I waste away: I cannot live forever; let me alone, for my days are but a breath.
verses.156: What is man, that you make much of him, or pay him any heed?
verses.157: You observe him with each new day and try him at every moment!
verses.158: How long will it be before you look away from me, and let me alone long enough to swallow my spittle?
verses.159: Though I have sinned, what can I do to you, O watcher of men?
verses.160: Why do you not pardon my offense, or take away my guilt? For soon I shall lie down in the dust; and should you seek me I shall then be gone. 1 [1] Drudgery: taken by some to refer to military service; cf also ⇒ Job 14:14. 2 [12] An allusion in poetic imagery to primeval chaos as a monstrous ocean vanquished by God at the world's creation. 3 [12-21] Job now speaks, not to his friend, but to God. verses.161: Bildad the Shuhite spoke out and said:
verses.162: How long will you utter such things? The words from your mouth are like a mighty wind!
verses.163: Does God pervert judgment, and does the Almighty distort justice?
verses.164: If your children have sinned against him and he has left them in the grip of their guilt,
verses.165: Still, if you yourself have recourse to God and make supplication to the Almighty,
verses.166: Should you be blameless and upright, surely now he will awake for you and restore your rightful domain;
verses.167: Your former state will be of little moment, for in time to come you will flourish indeed.
verses.168: If you inquire of the former generations, and give heed to the experience of the fathers
verses.169: (As we are but of yesterday and have no knowledge, because our days on earth are but a shadow),
verses.170: Will they not teach you and tell you and utter their words of understanding?
verses.171: 1 Can the papyrus grow up without mire? Can the reed grass flourish without water?
verses.172: While it is yet green and uncut, it withers quicker than any grass.
verses.173: So is the end of everyone who forgets God, and so shall the hope of the godless man perish.
verses.174: His confidence is but a gossamer thread and his trust is a spider's web.
verses.175: He shall rely upon his family, but it shall not last; he shall cling to it, but it shall not endure.
verses.176: He is full of sap before sunrise, and beyond his garden his shoots go forth;
verses.177: About a heap of stones are his roots entwined; among the rocks he takes hold.
verses.178: Yet if one tears him from his place, it will disown him: "I have never seen you!"
verses.179: There he lies rotting beside the road, and out of the soil another sprouts.
verses.180: Behold, God will not cast away the upright; neither will he take the hand of the wicked.
verses.181: Once more will he fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with rejoicing.
verses.182: They that hate you shall be clothed with shame, and the tent of the wicked shall be no more. 1 [11-13] As marsh plants need water, so man needs God. These verses are taken by some as a quotation from the teaching of the forefathers; cf ⇒ Job 8:10. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.184: I know well that it is so; but how can a man be justified before God?
verses.185: Should one wish to contend with him, he could not answer him once in a thousand times.
verses.186: God is wise in heart and mighty in strength; who has withstood him and remained unscathed?
verses.187: He removes the mountains before they know it; he overturns them in his anger.
verses.188: He shakes the earth out of its place, and the pillars beneath it tremble.
verses.189: He commands the sun, and it rises not; he seals up the stars.
verses.190: He alone stretches out the heavens and treads upon the crests of the sea.
verses.191: He made the Bear and Orion, the Pleiades and the constellations of the south;
verses.192: He does great things past finding out, marvelous things beyond reckoning.
verses.193: Should he come near me, I see him not; should he pass by, I am not aware of him;
verses.194: Should he seize me forcibly, who can say him nay? Who can say to him, "What are you doing?"
verses.195: 1 He is God and he does not relent; the helpers of Rahab bow beneath him.
verses.196: How much less shall I give him any answer, or choose out arguments against him!
verses.197: Even though I were right, I could not answer him, but should rather beg for what was due me.
verses.198: If I appealed to him and he answered my call, I could not believe that he would hearken to my words;
verses.199: With a tempest he might overwhelm me, and multiply my wounds without cause;
verses.200: He need not suffer me to draw breath, but might fill me with bitter griefs.
verses.201: If it be a question of strength, he is mighty; and if of judgment, who will call him to account?
verses.202: Though I were right, my own mouth might condemn me; were I innocent, he might put me in the wrong.
verses.203: Though I am innocent, I myself cannot know it; I despise my life.
verses.204: It is all one! therefore I say: Both the innocent and the wicked he destroys.
verses.205: When the scourge slays suddenly, he laughs at the despair of the innocent.
verses.206: The earth is given into the hands of the wicked; he covers the faces of its judges. If it is not he, who then is it?
verses.207: My days are swifter than a runner, they flee away; they see no happiness;
verses.208: They shoot by like skiffs of reed, like an eagle swooping upon its prey.
verses.209: If I say: I will forget my complaining, I will lay aside my sadness and be of good cheer,
verses.210: 2 Then I am in dread of all my pains; I know that you will not hold me innocent.
verses.211: If I must be accounted guilty, why then should I strive in vain?
verses.212: If I should wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with lye,
verses.213: Yet you would plunge me in the ditch, so that my garments would abhor me.
verses.214: For he is not a man like myself, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.
verses.215: Would that there were an arbiter between us, who could lay his hand upon us both
verses.216: and withdraw his rod from me. Would that his terrors did not frighten me;
verses.217: that I might speak without being afraid of him. Since this is not the case with me, 1 [13] Rehab: cf ⇒ Job 26:12. See note on ⇒ Psalm 89:11. 2 [28-31] You: refers to God. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.218: 1 I loathe my life. I will give myself up to complaint; I will speak from the bitterness of my soul.
verses.219: I will say to God: Do not put me in the wrong! Let me know why you oppose me.
verses.220: Is it a pleasure for you to oppress, to spurn the work of your hands, and smile on the plan of the wicked?
verses.221: Have you eyes of flesh? Do you see as man sees?
verses.222: Are your days as the days of a mortal, and are your years as a man's lifetime,
verses.223: That you seek for guilt in me and search after my sins,
verses.224: Even though you know that I am not wicked, and that none can deliver me out of your hand?
verses.225: Your hands have formed me and fashioned me; will you then turn and destroy me?
verses.226: Oh, remember that you fashioned me from clay! Will you then bring me down to dust again?
verses.227: Did you not pour me out as milk, and thicken me like cheese?
verses.228: With skin and flesh you clothed me, with bones and sinews knit me together.
verses.229: Grace and favor you granted me, and your providence has preserved my spirit.
verses.230: Yet these things you have hidden in your heart; I know that they are your purpose:
verses.231: If I should sin, you would keep a watch against me, and from my guilt you would not absolve me.
verses.232: If I should be wicked, alas for me! if righteous, I dare not hold up my head, filled with ignominy and sodden with affliction!
verses.233: Should it lift up, you hunt me like a lion: repeatedly you show your wondrous power against me,
verses.234: You renew your attack upon me and multiply your harassment of me; in waves your troops come against me.
verses.235: Why then did you bring me forth from the womb? I should have died and no eye have seen me.
verses.236: I should be as though I had never lived; I should have been taken from the womb to the grave.
verses.237: Are not the days of my life few? Let me alone, that I may recover a little
verses.238: Before I go whence I shall not return, to the land of darkness and of gloom,
verses.239: The black, disordered land where darkness is the only light. 1 [1] I loathe my life: this is the first verse of Job 10. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.240: And Zophar the Naamathite spoke out and said:
verses.241: Should not the man of many words be answered, or must the garrulous man necessarily be right?
verses.242: Shall your babblings keep men silent, and shall you deride and no one give rebuke?
verses.243: Shall you say: "My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your sight"?
verses.244: But oh, that God would speak, and open his lips against you,
verses.245: And tell you that the secrets of wisdom are twice as effective: So you might learn that God will make you answer for your guilt.
verses.246: Can you penetrate the designs of God? Dare you vie with the perfection of the Almighty?
verses.247: It is higher than the heavens; what can you do? It is deeper than the nether world; what can you know?
verses.248: It is longer than the earth in measure, and broader than the sea.
verses.249: If he seize and imprison or call to judgment, who then can say him nay?
verses.250: For he knows the worthlessness of men and sees iniquity; will he then ignore it?
verses.251: Will empty man then gain understanding, and the wild jackass be made docile?
verses.252: If you set your heart aright and stretch out your hands toward him,
verses.253: If you remove all iniquity from your conduct, and let not injustice dwell in your tent,
verses.254: Surely then you may lift up your face in innocence; you may stand firm and unafraid.
verses.255: For then you shall forget your misery, or recall it like waters that have ebbed away.
verses.256: Then your life shall be brighter than the noonday; its gloom shall become as the morning,
verses.257: And you shall be secure, because there is hope; you shall look round you and lie down in safety,
verses.258: and you shall take your rest with none to disturb. Many shall entreat your favor,
verses.259: but the wicked, looking on, shall be consumed with envy. Escape shall be cut off from them, they shall wait to expire. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.261: No doubt you are the intelligent folk, and with you wisdom shall die!
verses.262: But I have intelligence as well as you; for who does not know such things as these?
verses.263: 1 I have become the sport of my neighbors: "The one whom God answers when he calls upon him, The just, the perfect man," is a laughing-stock;
verses.264: The undisturbed esteem my downfall a disgrace such as awaits unsteady feet;
verses.265: Yet the tents of robbers are prosperous, and those who provoke God are secure.
verses.266: But now ask the beasts to teach you, and the birds of the air to tell you;
verses.267: Or the reptiles on earth to instruct you, and the fish of the sea to inform you.
verses.268: Which of all these does not know that the hand of God has done this?
verses.269: In his hand is the soul of every living thing, and the life breath of all mankind.
verses.270: Does not the ear judge words as the mouth tastes food?
verses.271: So with old age is wisdom, and with length of days understanding.
verses.272: With him are wisdom and might; his are counsel and understanding.
verses.273: If he breaks a thing down, there is no rebuilding; if he imprisons a man, there is no release.
verses.274: He holds back the waters and there is drought; he sends them forth and they overwhelm the land.
verses.275: With him are strength and prudence; the misled and the misleaders are his.
verses.276: He sends counselors away barefoot, and of judges he makes fools.
verses.277: 2 He loosens the bonds imposed by kings and leaves but a waistcloth to bind the king's own loins.
verses.278: and lets their never-failing waters flow away.
verses.279: He silences the trusted adviser, and takes discretion from the aged.
verses.280: He breaks down the barriers of the streams
verses.281: The recesses of the darkness he discloses, and brings the gloom forth to the light.
verses.282: He makes nations great and he destroys them; he spreads peoples abroad and he abandons them.
verses.283: He takes understanding from the leaders of the land,
verses.284: till they grope in the darkness without light; he makes them stagger like drunken men. 1 [4-5] The Hebrew is somewhat obscure, but the general sense is that the wicked mock at the pious when the latter appear to be abandoned by God; cf ⇒ Psalm 22:7-9; ⇒ Matthew 27:39-43. 2 [18] (18)Waistcloth . . . loins: he reduces kings to the condition of slaves, who wear only a cloth wrapped about the waist. verses.285: Lo, all this my eye has seen; my ear has heard and perceived it.
verses.286: What you know, I also know; I fall not short of you.
verses.287: But I would speak with the Almighty; I wish to reason with God.
verses.288: You are glossing over falsehoods and offering vain remedies, every one of you!
verses.289: Oh, that you would be altogether silent! This for you would be wisdom.
verses.290: Hear now the rebuke I shall utter and listen to the reproof from my lips.
verses.291: Is it for God that you speak falsehood? Is it for him that you utter deceit?
verses.292: Is it for him that you show partiality? Do you play advocate on behalf of God?
verses.293: Will it be well when he shall search you out? Would you impose on him as one does on men?
verses.294: He will openly rebuke you if even in secret you show partiality.
verses.295: Surely will his majesty affright you and the dread of him fall upon you.
verses.296: Your reminders are ashy maxims, your fabrications are mounds of clay.
verses.297: Be silent, let me alone! that I may speak and give vent to my feelings.
verses.298: 1 I will carry my flesh between my teeth, and take my life in my hand.
verses.299: Slay me though he might, I will wait for him; I will defend my conduct before him.
verses.300: And this shall be my salvation, that no impious man can come into his presence.
verses.301: Pay careful heed to my speech, and give my statement a hearing.
verses.302: Behold, I have prepared my case, I know that I am in the right.
verses.303: If anyone can make a case against me, then I shall be silent and die.
verses.304: 2 These things only do not use against me, then from your presence I need not hide:
verses.305: Withdraw your hand far from me, and let not the terror of you frighten me.
verses.306: Then call me, and I will respond; or let me speak first, and answer me.
verses.307: What are my faults and my sins? My misdeeds and my sins make known to me!
verses.308: Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy?
verses.309: Will you harass a wind-driven leaf, or pursue a withered straw?
verses.310: For you draw up bitter indictments against me, and punish in me the faults of my youth.
verses.311: You put my feet in the stocks; you watch all my paths and trace out all my footsteps.

But the current Hebrew text of this line is probably corrupt. 2 [22] Divine: possessing God's attributes of judgment and authority to punish. 3 [23-24] Job regards what he is about to say as so important that he wishes it recorded in a permanent manner. 4 [25, 27] The meaning of this passage is obscure because the original text has been poorly preserved and the ancient versions do not agree among themselves. It is certain that Job expresses his belief in a future vindication by God (called here in the Hebrew "Goel"), but the time and manner of this vindication are undefined. In the Vulgate Job is made to indicate a belief in physical resurrection after death, but the Hebrew and the other ancient versions are less specific. A young man, he impetuously and impatiently upbraids Job for his boldness toward God, and the three friends for not successfully answering Job. He undertakes to defend God's absolute justice and to explain more clearly why there is suffering. verses.866: But now that you have done otherwise, God's anger punishes, nor does he show concern that a man will die.
verses.867: Yet Job to no purpose opens his mouth, and without knowledge multiplies words. 1 [4] A reply to you: Elihu refers to Job's statement that the innocent suffer as much as the wicked, and especially to Eliphaz's words in ⇒ Job 22:2-3. 2 [14-15] The text here is uncertain. It seems to indicate that Job should have realized God's indifference is only apparent, and that, because he has not done so, God will punish him. verses.901: At this my heart trembles and leaps out of its place,
verses.902: 1 To hear his angry voice as it rumbles forth from his mouth!
verses.903: Everywhere under the heavens he sends it, with his lightning, to the ends of the earth.
verses.904: Again his voice roars - the majestic sound of his thunder.
verses.905: He does great things beyond our knowing; wonders past our searching out.
verses.906: For he says to the snow, "Fall to the earth"; likewise to his heavy, drenching rain.
verses.907: He shuts up all mankind indoors;
verses.908: the wild beasts take to cover and remain quietly in their dens.
verses.909: 2 Out of its chamber comes forth the tempest; from the north winds, the cold.
verses.910: With his breath God brings the frost, and the broad waters become congealed.
verses.911: With hail, also, the clouds are laden, as they scatter their flashes of light.
verses.912: 3 He it is who changes their rounds, according to his plans, in their task upon the surface of the earth,
verses.913: whether for punishment or mercy, as he commands.
verses.914: Hearken to this, O Job! Stand and consider the wondrous works of God!
verses.915: Do you know how God lays his commands upon them, and makes the light shine forth from his clouds?
verses.916: Do you know how the clouds are banked, the wondrous work of him who is perfect in knowledge?
verses.917: You, whom the streams of water fail when a calm from the south comes over the land,
verses.918: 4 Do you spread out with him the firmament of the skies, hard as a brazen mirror?
verses.919: Teach us then what we shall say to him; we cannot, for the darkness, make our plea.
verses.920: 5 Will he be told about it when I speak, or when a man says he is being destroyed?
verses.921: 6 Nay, rather, it is as the light which men see not while it is obscured among the clouds, till the wind comes by and sweeps the clouds away.
verses.922: 7 From the North the splendor comes, surrounding God's awesome majesty!
verses.923: The Almighty! we cannot discover him, pre-eminent in power and judgment; his great justice owes no one an accounting.
verses.924: Therefore men revere him, though none can see him, however wise their hearts. 1 [2] Voice: the thunder. 2 [9] Chamber: where it was popularly believed storms were kept enclosed. 3 [12] Their rounds: of rain ( ⇒ Job 36:27), of clouds (Job 36:29-30), of lightning and thunder ( ⇒ Job 36:32-33), of snow ( ⇒ Job 37:6), of winds ( ⇒ Job 37:9). 4 [18] The firmament . . . mirror: the ancients thought of the sky as a ceiling above which were the "upper waters" (cf ⇒ Genesis 1:6-7; ⇒ 7:11); when this ceiling became as hard as metal, the usual rain failed to fall on the earth (cf ⇒ Lev 26:19; ⇒ Deut 28:23). 5 [20] Will an angel bring this to God's attention? 6 [21] Even though God seems not to know our circumstances, he does know them, just as surely as the sun shines, unseen by man, behind the clouds. 7 [22] Now the storms of doubt and ignorance disappear, and from the North, used here as a symbol for God's mysterious abode, comes the splendor of the manifestation of God's majestic ways. verses.966: Do you know about the birth of the mountain goats, watch for the birth pangs of the hinds,
verses.967: Number the months that they must fulfill, and fix the time of their bringing forth?
verses.968: They crouch down and bear their young; they deliver their progeny in the desert.
verses.969: When their offspring thrive and grow, they leave and do not return.
verses.970: Who has given the wild ass his freedom, and who has loosed him from bonds?
verses.971: I have made the wilderness his home and the salt flats his dwelling.
verses.972: He scoffs at the uproar of the city, and hears no shouts of a driver.
verses.973: He ranges the mountains for pasture, and seeks out every patch of green.
verses.974: Will the wild ox consent to serve you, and to pass the nights by your manger?
verses.975: Will a rope bind him in the furrow, and will he harrow the valleys after you?
verses.976: Will you trust him for his great strength and leave to him the fruits of your toil?
verses.977: Can you rely on him to thresh out your grain and gather in the yield of your threshing floor?
verses.978: 1 The wings of the ostrich beat idly; her plumage is lacking in pinions.
verses.979: 2 When she leaves her eggs on the ground and deposits them in the sand,
verses.980: Unmindful that a foot may crush them, that the wild beasts may trample them,
verses.981: She cruelly disowns her young and ruthlessly makes nought of her brood;
verses.982: For God has withheld wisdom from her and has given her no share in understanding.
verses.983: Yet in her swiftness of foot she makes sport of the horse and his rider.
verses.984: 3 Do you give the horse his strength, and endow his neck with splendor?
verses.985: Do you make the steed to quiver while his thunderous snorting spreads terror?
verses.986: He jubilantly paws the plain and rushes in his might against the weapons.
verses.987: He laughs at fear and cannot be deterred; he turns not back from the sword.
verses.988: Around him rattles the quiver, flashes the spear and the javelin.
verses.989: Frenzied and trembling he devours the ground; he holds not back at the sound of the trumpet,
verses.990: but at each blast he cries, "Aha!" Even from afar he scents the battle, the roar of the chiefs and the shouting.
verses.991: Is it by your discernment that the hawk soars, that he spreads his wings toward the south?
verses.992: Does the eagle fly up at your command to build his nest aloft?
verses.993: On the cliff he dwells and spends the night, on the spur of the cliff or the fortress.
verses.994: From thence he watches for his prey; his eyes behold it afar off.
verses.995: His young ones greedily drink blood; where the slain are, there is he. 1 [13] The wings of the ostrich cannot raise her from the ground, but they help her to run swiftly. 2 [14-16] It was popularly believed that, because the ostrich laid her eggs on the sand, she was thereby cruelly abandoning them; cf ⇒ Lam 4:3. 3 [19-25] The famous description of a war horse. verses.1054: Then Job answered the LORD and said:
verses.1055: 1 I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be hindered.
verses.1056: I have dealt with great things that I do not understand; things too wonderful for me, which I cannot know.
verses.1058: I had heard of you by word of mouth, but now my eye has seen you.
verses.1059: Therefore I disown what I have said, and repent in dust and ashes.
verses.1060: 2 And it came to pass after the LORD had spoken these words to Job, that the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "I am angry with you and with your two friends; for you have not spoken rightly concerning me, as has my servant Job.
verses.1061: 3 Now, therefore, take seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up a holocaust for yourselves; and let my servant Job pray for you; for his prayer I will accept, not to punish you severely. For you have not spoken rightly concerning me, as has my servant Job."
verses.1062: Then Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite, went and did as the LORD had commanded them. And the LORD accepted the intercession of Job.
verses.1063: Also, the LORD restored the prosperity of Job, after he had prayed for his friends; the LORD even gave to Job twice as much as he had before.
verses.1064: 4 Then all his brethren and his sisters came to him, and all his former acquaintances, and they dined with him in his house. They condoled with him and comforted him for all the evil which the LORD had brought upon him; and each one gave him a piece of money and a gold ring.
verses.1065: Thus the LORD blessed the latter days of Job more than his earlier ones. For he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she-asses.
verses.1066: And he had seven sons and three daughters,
verses.1067: 5 of whom he called the first Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
verses.1068: 6 In all the land no other women were as beautiful as the daughters of Job; and their father gave them an inheritance among their brethren.
verses.1069: 7 After this, Job lived a hundred and forty years; and he saw his children, his grandchildren, and even his great-grandchildren.
verses.1070: Then Job died, old and full of years. 1 [2-6] In the current Hebrew text, this final utterance of Job is interrupted by words ascribed to God ( ⇒ Job 42:3-4) which are in large part a duplication of ⇒ Job 38:2-3. 2 [7] The three friends of Job (Elihu is ignored in the Epilogue) are criticized by the LORD because they had (even though in good faith) leveled false charges against him. 3 [8] Job becomes the intercessor for his friends, as were other great Old Testament characters, e.g., Abraham and Moses, and as our Lord would be, whom he prefigured. Seven: a symbolic number. 4 [11] A piece of money: the term is the same as that used in ⇒ Genesis 33:19; ⇒ Joshua 24:32. Gold ring: for the nose or ear. 5 [14] Job's daughters had names symbolic of their charms: Jemimah, dove; Keziah, precious perfume (cf ⇒ Psalm 45:9); Kerenhappuch, cosmetic jar-more precisely, a container for a black powder that was used like modern mascara. 6 [15] Ordinarily daughters did not inherit property unless there were no sons; cf ⇒ Numbers 27:1-11. 7 [16] As his other rewards were twice as much as he had before ( ⇒ Job 42:10) so Job's hundred and forty years were double the expected span of human life; cf ⇒ Psalm 90:10.
